data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's distinguishing evidence is circular and lacks a causal mechanism. It defines genuine gain as the panel's error set being a strict subset of the expert's within the consistency-requiring partition, but partition membership is itself inferred from triggered checklist-item count — a proxy the target admits can be uncorrelated with actual complexity. There is no independent causal grounding for the partition, so the 'strict subset' criterion can be satisfied artifactually by relabeling cases. The target provides no mechanism explaining why checklist coarseness causes boundary errors or why expert intuition causes consistency errors, so the error-set comparison cannot distinguish genuine reliability gain from an artifact of the partitioning scheme.
